subject: Post-call: VaultBank control-plane & air-gap feasibility — next technical tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: VaultBank control-plane & air-gap feasibility — next technical tests

Hi team — thanks again for carving out time earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next tests so everyone is aligned:

- Ask: VaultBank wants a private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) with a customer-managed control plane or fully air-gapped capability for sensitive workloads.
- Competitive context: you mentioned comparing Redwood to hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS/Azure) and a few inference API vendors — key differentiators we highlighted were private control plane option, optional on-prem package, and explicit network peering/edge routing controls.

Proposed next technical tests (short list):
1) Network connectivity verification: we provide a sample VPC diagram and a small PoC config for VPC endpoints (attached). You run a connectivity smoke test (curl / curl over private link) and share tcpdump/snippet.
2) Control-plane reachability validation: show the control-plane-only handshake (metadata update) over a mutual TLS channel; we can run a constrained test that logs only connection attempts.
3) Air-gap feasibility checklist: the team asked what fully air-gapped would look like — we attached a feasibility checklist. Laura, can you add a note on packaging size and on-prem installer options?
4) Latency baseline: short generator test against a pinned model variant from your on-prem node vs Redwood Dedicated to compare p95 latency and KV cache behavior.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-architecture.pdf (diagram), poa-vpc-endpoints-sample.txt (curl examples), airgap-feasibility-checklist.xlsx

Next steps / ask of VaultBank / CloudScale: let us know preferred windows for the technical run (2–3 hour window), share an internal network contact who can accept our sample traffic, and any firewall egress rules to account for.

I’ll loop in Laura for technical details and Rishi for any contractual notes on the PoC.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Karthik — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying items from procurement and ops: 

1) Control plane: we need to understand whether the control plane can be customer-hosted (we run it in our VPC) or whether Redwood requires egress to a Redwood-managed control plane for telemetry and updates. What telemetry is mandatory?
2) Air-gap: the checklist looks helpful. For a fully air-gapped install, will we still need to import licensing artifacts or any signed binaries from Redwood? If so, we need a chain-of-custody and signing guarantee.
3) Hyperscaler comparison: our cloud infra team is worried that moving to hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints means losing KV cache persistence between restarts. Can you confirm Redwood’s cache persistence options in private deployments vs the hyperscaler solutions we’ve looked at?

Ops (cc’d): please advise on who will accept the test traffic and whether our egress rules can permit the sample handshake ports.

Procurement note: also include any PoC credit/discount language up front so we can prepare approvals.

Regards,
Maya Rao

procurement@vaultbank.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: VaultBank Procurement <procurement@vaultbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudScale Ops <ops@cloudscale.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: VaultBank control-plane & air-gap feasibility — next technical tests

Hi Maya / team — Laura here (Solutions Engineering). Answers inline and next steps: 

1) Control plane hosting: Redwood supports two models for private deployments:
   - Customer-managed control plane: we provide the control-plane container images and orchestration manifests; you deploy them in your VPC (no egress required for control-plane core functions).
   - Redwood-managed control plane (optional): we host the control plane and maintain updates; in that case we require TLS egress for heartbeat + attestations (can be restricted to specific IPs and mTLS).

   Mandatory telemetry: minimal health heartbeats and failure alerts can be optionally disabled for fully isolated air-gapped installs. For our supported on-prem air-gap, updates and model artifacts are vendor-provided via signed bundles that you import manually — we can provide signing certificates and a verification tool.

2) Air-gap packaging: Fully air-gapped flow requires a short import process: signed artifact bundles (models + runtime), a license token that is offline-validated, and optional HSM-backed key import for encryption-at-rest. We provide a chain-of-custody template and signing cert fingerprints. See attached checklist for exact steps.

3) KV cache / persistence: In Redwood Private (customer-hosted) you can persist KV cache to local disk or to an NFS/S3-compatible store in your VPC — that provides cache warm-starts after restarts. Hyperscaler-managed endpoints often do not expose persistent KV between cold starts (depends on the vendor); our private offering is designed to preserve cache state for bursty financial workloads.

Attached: redwood-vpc-architecture.pdf (network and peering patterns), airgap-feasibility-checklist.xlsx (detailed steps), poa-vpc-endpoints-sample.txt (sample curl + iptables rules).

Recommended technical run: Friday 2026-09-24 09:00–11:00 PDT (we can do 09:00–12:00 if you want extra buffer). Test plan will include connectivity, mTLS handshake capture, and a 100-request latency baseline (p95).

If you want an on-site installer for air-gapped import we can schedule a packaged delivery; lead time ~2 weeks depending on signing and compliance approvals.

Laura Bennett
